body.heading: Why small memories matter
paragraphs: Phone reminders handle birthdays for everyone. What touches people is the unlisted stuff: asking how the interview went, remembering that March is a hard month, knowing how they take their tea.
Remembering says: you were paying attention when it would have been easy not to. That is rare, and people feel it immediately.

body.heading: It is a system, not a talent
paragraphs: The friend who remembers is usually not blessed with a magical memory — they write things down. A note in your phone after a conversation takes ten seconds and pays off for years.
Start with three people. Learn one small thing about each — a date, a worry, a hope — and follow up on it once. You will be surprised how much it means.

description: Remembering the small things — the exam date, the dog's name, the hard anniversary — is a quiet superpower.
